First, recall that

$$
{lim}_{s\to 2}f(s)=⟨{lim}_{s\to 2}\frac{5}{{e}^{s-2}},\,{lim}_{s\to 2}3\operatorname{cos}⁡(4-2s),\,{lim}_{s\to 2}\,({s}^{3}-5)⟩.
$$

Now, we find the limits one by one.

- For the first component, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 2}\frac{5}{{e}^{s-2}} & =\frac{5}{{e}^{0}}=5.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 2}3\operatorname{cos}⁡(4-2s) & =3{lim}_{s\to 2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4-2s) \\  & =3\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(4-2(0)) \\  & =3\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡0 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the third component, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 2}\,({s}^{3}-5) & ={2}^{3}-5=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${lim}_{s\to 2}f(s)=⟨5,3,3⟩.$

Finally, the limit of $‖f(s)‖$ as $s$ approaches $2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{s\to 2}‖f(s)‖ & =‖{lim}_{s\to 2}f(s)‖ \\  & =‖⟨5,3,3⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{25+9+9} \\  & =\sqrt{43}.\end{aligned}
$$
